title: Deploying Zscaler Client Connector with Jamf Pro for macOS

blocks.text: This guide is for admins only. If you are an end user, contact your organization's administrator for deployment-related details.

With Jamf Pro, you can deploy Zscaler Client Connector for your macOS devices. Before deploying Zscaler Client Connector from the Jamf Pro web application (Jamf Pro), download the .pkg file from the Zscaler Client Connector App Store first.

blocks.item: Step 1: Download the Zscaler Client Connector .pkg file
To deploy Zscaler Client Connector using Jamf Pro, you must obtain a .pkg file from the Zscaler Admin Console.
To download the Zscaler Client Connector .pkg file:
In the Zscaler Admin Console, go to Infrastructure > Common Resources > Deployment > Platform Releases.
On the New Releases tab, select macOS.
Download the .pkg file.
Step 2: Deploy Zscaler Client Connector from Jamf Pro
To deploy Zscaler Client Connector on your macOS devices from Jamf Pro:
In Jamf Pro, go to Settings > Computer Management > Packages​​​​​​.
Under the General section, click Choose File to upload the .pkg file.
See image.
Click Save.
In the left-side navigation, go to Computers > Policies.
In the Policies window, click New.
See image.
In the General section, choose the Trigger events and Execution frequency as needed in your environment.
See image.
Click Save.
In the left-side navigation, select Packages, and click Configure.
See image.
Click Add, and choose the .pkg file uploaded previously.
Click Save.
On the Scope tab, assign the .pkg to the applicable devices.
See image.
Click Save.

To reinstall the same version of Zscaler Client Connector for a specific device or user, go to the computer's history and select Flush All for all the Policy Logs. Alternatively, you can delete the device or user from Jamf Pro and reinstall via the client.
Step 3: (Optional) Configure a Custom Settings Profile
You can use a property list (PLIST) file to set values for various configuration keys in Jamf Pro. To configure a custom settings profile in Jamf Pro:
In Jamf Pro, go to Computers > Configuration Profiles.
Click Application & Custom Settings to expand the section.
Select Upload, then click Add (+).
See image.
In the Upload section:
Preference Domain: Enter com.zscaler.installparams
Property List: Enter the following PLIST file and edit Zscaler configuration parameters and their corresponding values per your organization's needs.

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd"> <plist version="1.0"> <dict> <key>installation-parameters</key> <dict> <key>cloudName</key> <string>zscalertwo</string> <key>deviceToken</key> <string></string> <key>hideAppUIOnLaunch</key> <string>0</string> <key>launchTray</key> <string>1</string> <key>policyToken</key> <string> <policy token from app></string> <key>strictEnforcement</key> <string>0</string> <key>userDomain</key> <string>zexample.com</string> <key>externalRedirect</key> <string>false</string> <key>externalDeviceId</key> <string>device123</string> <key>userName</key> <string>test11</string> <key>enableFips</key> <string>0</string> </dict> </dict> </plist>
See image.
In the Scope section, set Targets, Limitations, and Exclusions to bind the configuration profile to particular devices and users.
Step 4: (Optional) Configure a Certificate Configuration Profile

If you use Internet & SaaS and you want to perform SSL inspection, you must configure a certificate profile to push the Certificate Authority (CA) certificate required for SSL inspection. You can use the default Zscaler CA certificate or a custom Root or Intermediate CA certificate. To learn more, see Choosing the CA Certificate for SSL Inspection and Certificate Pinning and SSL Inspection.
To configure a certificate configuration profile:
(Optional) Download the Zscaler CA Certificate.
To download the certificate:
In the Zscaler Admin Console, go to Policies > Common Configuration > SSL/TLS Inspection > SSL/TLS Inspection Intermediate Certificate.
Click the Edit icon corresponding to the Zscaler Intermediate CA Certificate.
The View Zscaler Intermediate CA Certificate window appears.
In the View Zscaler Intermediate CA Certificate window, under the Root Certificate field, click Download.
The root certificate is downloaded as a ZIP file.
Navigate to the ZscalerRootCerts.zip file and unzip it and rename the file extension to .cer.
Configure the Certificate Profile.
To configure the profile:
In Jamf Pro, go to Computers > Configuration Profiles.
Select New and under General, enter a name for the configuration profile.
Select Certificate and click Configure.
See image.
Enter a name for the certificate.
In the Select Certificate option, click Upload.
Click Upload to upload the certificate previously downloaded.
See image.
Enable the Allow all apps access option and Save the profile.
See image.
In the Scope section, set Targets, Limitations, and Exclusions to bind the configuration profile to particular devices and users.
Step 5: (Optional) Configure Traffic Interception
Zscaler Client Connector can intercept traffic locally using either Route-based Interception or Transparent Proxy-based Interception.

Transparent Proxy-based Interception uses the macOS Transparent Network Proxy Extension to intercept traffic. The TRPTunnel Network Extension (com.zscaler.zscaler.TRPTunnel) is used for traffic interception and application bypass and has the following benefits:
No reliance on routing tables
Better performance
Zscaler Tunnel (Z-Tunnel) 2.0 compatibility with third-party VPN clients
Removes the need for inbound firewall rules if not using machine tunnels

If machine tunnels are used with Transparent Proxy-based Interception mode enabled, inbound traffic to ZscalerTunnel must be enabled in your firewall rules to allow access to Private Access apps. In addition, be sure to disable FileVault to allow Private Access connections before a user logs in to Zscaler Client Connector on their device. To learn more, see Zscaler Client Connector Processes to Allowlist
Transparent Proxy-based Interception is supported on Zscaler Client Connector version 4.5.2 and later for macOS Tahoe 26.2 and later with the following exceptions:

table: Supported on Zscaler Client Connector version 4.8 and later
Supported on Zscaler Client Connector version 4.7 and later
Supported on Zscaler Client Connector version 4.5.2.372 and later, 4.7.0.380 and later, 4.8.0.281 and later, and 4.10.0.36 and later
Supported with domain-name-based Private Access apps on Zscaler Client Connector version 4.5.2.355 and later, 4.7.0.351 and later, and 4.8.0.252 and later

Some macOS applications have known compatibility issues with Apple's Network Extensions and you might experience interoperability issues. To learn more, see the Known Issues List on the Zscaler Support Portal.

blocks.item: When configuring Zscaler Client Connector with Transparent Proxy-based Interception, bypass video and audio UDP streams from collaboration applications which rely on STUN (e.g., Slack, WebEx) along with STUN using Predefined IP-Based Application Bypass, Custom IP-Based Application Bypass, or IP Exclusions in app profiles. You can bypass STUN protocol by specifying TCP and UDP port 3478.
To configure traffic interception, you must apply the following high-level steps:
Deploy a Configuration Profile to macOS Devices (Transparent Proxy-based Traffic Interception Only)
Create a Forwarding Profile and Enable Z-Tunnel 2.0
Create an App Profile
Create a macOS app profile or edit an existing one.
Under General, select the forwarding profile you configured in the previous step and enable the Reconnect Tunnel on System Wakeup option.
See image.
If you are configuring Transparent Proxy-based Traffic Interception, under Traffic Steering > Advanced, enable the Enable Transparent Proxy-based Traffic Interception option.
See image.

Choose either of the following two options to create a configuration profile to deploy Transparent Proxy-based Traffic Interception. If you also need to deploy Application Bypass, use the Import a Preconfigured mobileconfig File Into Jamf option because Jamf Pro doesn't support arrays in custom data types at this time.
Manually Create a Configuration Profile in Jamf Pro
Import a Preconfigured mobileconfig File Into Jamf Pro
In Jamf Pro, go to Computers > Configuration Profiles.
From the left-side navigation, go to General, click New and enter a name for the configuration profile.
Go to System Extensions and click Configure.
See image.
In the System Extensions section:
Display Name: Enter Zscaler TRP Network Extension.
System Extension type: Select Non-removable system extensions from UI to prevent users from disabling Zscaler Client Connector forwarding.
The non-removable system extension functionality is supported only on macOS Sequoia (15) and later, so if you are deploying to an earlier version of macOS, select Allowed instead.
Team Identifier: Enter PCBCQZJ7S7.
Non-removable system extensions from UI: Click Add (+) and enter com.zscaler.zscaler.TRPTunnel.
Click Save.
See image.
From the left-side navigation, go to VPN and click Configure.
See image.
In the VPN section:
Connection Name: Enter Zscaler TRP Tunnel.
VPN Type: Select VPN.
Connection Type: Select Custom SSL.
Identifier: Enter com.zscaler.zscaler
Server: Enter Zscaler server.
Provider Bundle Identifier: Enter com.zscaler.zscaler.TRPTunnel
See image.
Provider Type: Select App-proxy.
Provider Designated Requirement: Enter identifier "com.zscaler.zscaler.TRPTunnel" and anchor apple generic.
See image.
Select the checkbox for Prohibit users from disabling on-demand VPN settings
Click Save.
In the Scope section, set Targets, Limitations, and Exclusions to bind the configuration profile to particular devices and users.
In Jamf Pro, go to Computers > Configuration Profiles.
Download the mobileconfig file.
Click Upload > Choose File and upload the mobileconfig file.
See image.
The General, VPN, and System Extensions sections are auto-populated.
In the Scope section, set Targets, Limitations, and Exclusions to bind the configuration profile to particular devices and users.
Create a forwarding profile.
Select Z-Tunnel 2.0 when configuring a forwarding profile with Tunnel mode and the packet filter driver is enabled.
Configure bypasses for Z-Tunnel 2.0 in Zscaler Client Connector profile. To learn more, see Best Practices for Adding Bypasses for Z-Tunnel 2.0.

Under Forwarding Profile Action for ZIA, ensure that the Drop IPv6 in Dual Stack Network option is disabled so that IPv6 traffic isn't discarded after it has been generated by macOS, which could lead to unexpected behavior for applications and services that do not gracefully fall back to IPv4.
See image.
Step 6: (Optional) Configure Tunnel Parameters
You can configure the following tunnel parameters for Zscaler Client Connector with Jamf Pro.
Prevent DNS Caching
This configuration setting is only supported with Route-based Traffic Interception and is not compatible with Transparent Proxy-based Traffic Interception.
You can use a property list (PLIST) file to set tunnel parameters, allowing DNS caching to be cleared from users' devices. To configure tunnel parameters in Jamf Pro:
In Jamf Pro, go to Computers > Configuration Profiles.
In General, select New to create a new profile and enter a name for the profile.
Click Application & Custom Settings to expand the section and click Upload > Add.
See image.
In the Upload section:
Preference Domain: Enter com.zscaler.tunnelparams
Property List: Add the following PLIST:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd"> <plist version="1.0"> <dict> <key>tunnel-parameters</key> <dict> <key>clearDnsCacheOnT2Start</key> <string>1</string> </dict> </dict> </plist>
If the clearDnsCacheOnT2Start parameter is enabled, on Tunnel restart, DNS caches are cleared from the device. Enter 1 to enable, or 0 to disable.
See image.
Click Save.
In the Scope section, set Targets, Limitations, and Exclusions to bind the configuration profile to particular devices and users.
If you are already logged in to Zscaler Client Connector, exit and relaunch the app or click Restart Service in the More window of the app.
Bring Zscaler Client Connector Window to the Foreground
You can use a property list (PLIST) to set tunnel parameters, allowing you to bring the Zscaler Client Connector window to the foreground.
To bring Zscaler Client Connector window to the foreground:
In Jamf Pro, go to Computers > Configuration Profiles.
If you already have an existing configuration profile to control a particular Zscaler Client Connector behavior (e.g., prevent DNS caching), select the profile and click Edit.
Expand the Application & Custom Settings section and click Upload > Add.
In the Upload section:
Preference Domain: Enter com.zscaler.tunnelparams
Property List: Add the following PLIST:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd"> <plist version="1.0"> <dict> <key>tunnel-parameters</key> <dict> <key>zccToForegroundDuringAuth</key> <string>1</string> </dict> </dict> </plist>
If zccToForegroundDuringAuth parameter is enabled, it brings the Zscaler Client Connector window to the foreground during WebView-based authentication. Enter 1 to enable, or 0 to disable.

The following image combines the PLIST for both clearDnsCacheOnT2Start and zccToForegroundDuringAuth parameters. You can configure settings for both parameters together if you haven't already configured settings for clearDnsCacheOnT2Start.
See image.
Click Save.
In the Scope section, set Targets, Limitations, and Exclusions to bind the configuration profile to particular devices and users.
If you are already logged in to Zscaler Client Connector, exit and relaunch the app or click Restart Service in the More window of the app.
Step 7: (Optional) Configure a Custom VPN Profile for Private Access VPN (for Legacy Apps)

This configuration setting is supported with Route-based Traffic Interception on all supported releases of Zscaler Client Connector for macOS and with Transparent Proxy-based Traffic Interception on Zscaler Client Connector version 4.8 and later for macOS.
You can use a property list (PLIST) file to configure a custom VPN profile for Private Access VPN (for Legacy Apps) in Jamf Pro:
In Jamf Pro, go to Computers > Configuration Profiles.
In General, select New to create a new profile and enter a name for the profile.
From the left-side navigation, go to VPN and click Configure.
See image.
In the VPN section:
Connection Name: Enter Zscaler ZPA VPN.
VPN Type: Select VPN.
Connection Type: Select Custom SSL.
Identifier: Enter com.zscaler.zscaler
Server: Enter Zscaler server.
Provider Bundle Identifier: Enter com.zscaler.zscaler.pktfilter
See image.
Provider Type: Select Packet-tunnel.
Provider Designated Requirement: Enter identifier "com.zscaler.zscaler.pktfilter" and anchor apple generic.
Prohibit users from disabling on-demand VPN settings: Select this checkbox.
See image.
To ensure a seamless user experience, configure the system extension in Jamf Pro and activate it. To learn more, see Configuration Profile for Auto Approval of Zscaler System Extension.
Click Save.
In the Scope section, set Targets, Limitations, and Exclusions to bind the configuration profile to particular devices and users.
Step 8: (Optional) Configure Full Disk Access for Endpoint DLP
Zscaler Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (DLP) requires full disk access for proper operation. Choose either of the following two options to create a DLP profile with Jamf Pro to allow full disk access.
Manually Create a Configuration Profile in Jamf Pro
To configure a full disk access for Endpoint DLP in Jamf Pro:
a. Create a general profile.
b. Configure privacy preferences for policy control.
c. Configure notification settings.
Go to Computers > Configuration Profiles.
Click New.
For the General section:
Name: Enter ZDP.
Description: (Optional) Enter a brief explanation of the profile.
Click Save.
See image.
On the Options tab, click the Privacy Preferences Policy Control > Configure.

Click Add (+) (located in the upper right-hand corner of the pane) to add a new app to the Privacy Preferences section. Repeat this step for the identifiers listed in the following table in the App Access section:

table: identifier "com.zscaler.zdp.pd" and anchor apple generic and certificate 1[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.2.6] /* exists */ and certificate leaf[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.1.13] /* exists */ and certificate leaf[subject.OU] = PCBCQZJ7S7

identifier "com.zscaler.zdp.esd" and anchor apple generic and certificate 1[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.2.6] /* exists */ and certificate leaf[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.1.13] /* exists */ and certificate leaf[subject.OU] = PCBCQZJ7S7

identifier "com.zscaler.zdp.agent" and anchor apple generic and certificate 1[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.2.6] /* exists */ and certificate leaf[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.1.13] /* exists */ and certificate leaf[subject.OU] = PCBCQZJ7S7

blocks.item: Click Save.
See image.
On the Options tab, click the Privacy Preferences Policy Control > Configure.
From the left-side navigation, click the Notifications section.
Click Add to add a new notification.
App Name: Enter zdpagent.
Bundle ID: Enter com.zscaler.zdp.agent.
For Notifications, select Enable.
Banner alert type: Select Persistent from the drop-down menu.
Notifications in Notification Center: Select Display from the drop-down menu.
Play sound for notifications: Select Enable.
See image.
Import a Preconfigured mobileconfig File Into Jamf
In Jamf Pro, go to Computers > Configuration Profiles.
Download the ZDP.mobileconfig file.
You must remove any existing Zscaler Data Protection (ZDP) mobile device management (MDM) profiles before uploading a new profile.
Click the Upload button > Choose File and upload the ZDP.mobileconfig file.
See image.
Click Save.
See image.
You can configure managed login items to prevent users from disabling Zscaler Client Connector on their own devices. To configure managed login items in Jamf Pro:
In Jamf Pro, go to Computers > Configuration Profiles.
Select Managed Login Items.
See image.
Click Add for each of the following Rule Types and Rule Values:
Bundle Identifier: The bundle ID.
Bundle Identifier Prefix: A part of the bundle identifier reflecting the developer or organization.
Label: A descriptive name for an app or an element in the app's UI or settings.
Label Prefix: Used to group or categorize labels.
Team Identifier: A unique identifier for the developer team or organization within the Apple ecosystem. Applies to all of the configured rules. Enter PCBCQZJ7S7.
Rule comment: (Optional) Enter a comment for the rule.
See image.
Click Save.
See image.
In the Scope section, set Targets, Limitations, and Exclusions to bind the configuration profile to particular devices and users.
Step 9: (Optional) Configure Managed Login Items
Step 10: (Optional) Configure Process-Based Application Bypass

Zscaler Client Connector supports configuring process-based application bypasses differently based on whether you intercept traffic using Route-based Interception or Transparent Proxy-based Interception and the Zscaler Client Connector version you use.

table: Set up in the Zscaler Admin Console

blocks.item: To add process-based application bypasses for macOS, use one of the following options based on the type of traffic interception and version of Zscaler Client Connector you use:
Deploy application bypass with Transparent Proxy-based Traffic Interception (Zscaler Client Connector version 4.8 and later)
To configure applications to bypass in the Zscaler Admin Console:
Define any applications and process that need to be bypassed. To learn more, see Adding Process-Based Applications to Bypass Traffic.
In the Zscaler Admin Console, go to Infrastructure > Connectors > Client > macOS.
On the App Profiles tab, click the Edit icon on the app profile you created in step 5.
Under Traffic Steering > App and IP Bypass > Global Bypasses, select the applications to bypass from the Process-Based Application Bypass using AdminUI drop-down menu.
See image.
Click Save.

Deploy application bypass with Route-based Traffic Interception (all Zscaler Client Connector versions) or Transparent Proxy-based Traffic Interception (Zscaler Client Connector version 4.7 and earlier)

Application Bypass is deployed using the VPN payload in a configuration profile and because the VPN payloads are different for Route-based Traffic Interception and Transparent Proxy-based Traffic Interception, the mobileconfig files differ based on traffic interception type in use.

You can use bundle identifiers for application identification. If your identifier has both a Team ID and a Bundle ID in it, enter them in the format <Team ID>.<Bundle ID>. For example: <string>UBF8T346G9.com.microsoft.teams</string>
Where:
UBF8T346G9 is the Team ID
com.microsoft.teams is the Bundle ID

To enter multiple processes or applications, you can add all the bundle identifiers using an array. As an example, to bypass all Zoom processes, modify the downloaded mobileconfig file's BypassAppProcesses key with the following:
<key>BypassAppProcesses</key> <array> <string>BJ4HAAB9B3.us.zoom.xos</string> <string>BJ4HAAB9B3.zoom.us.ZoomAudioDevice</string> </array>

If you use Transparent Proxy-based Traffic Interception, you can also use process paths for application identification (e.g., /opt/homebrew/Cellar/podman/5.7.0/libexec/podman/gvproxy). Applies only to Zscaler Client Connector version 4.5.2.121 and later for macOS and version 4.7.0.87 and later for macOS.
To configure a custom settings profile in Jamf Pro for the applications you want to bypass:
Step 1: Deploy a Configuration Profile to macOS Devices
Download one of the following files as a starting template, and edit the values in the <VendorConfig> section of the file based on your needs.
ZscalerSampleMobileConfig (Route-based) file for Route-based Traffic Interception
ZscalerSampleMobileConfig (Transparent Proxy-based) file for Transparent Proxy-based Traffic Interception
In Jamf Pro, go to Computers > Configuration Profiles.
Select Upload.
Upload the mobile config file.
To ensure a seamless user experience, configure the system extension in Jamf Pro and activate it. To learn more, see Configuration Profile for Auto Approval of Zscaler System Extension.
In the Scope section, set Targets, Limitations, and Exclusions to bind the configuration profile to particular devices and users.
Step 2: Enable Application Bypass in App Profiles
In the Zscaler Admin Console, go to Infrastructure > Connectors > Client > macOS.
On the App Profiles tab, click the Edit icon on the app profile you created in step 5.
Under Traffic Steering > App and IP Bypass > Global Bypasses, enable the Process-Based Application Bypass using MDM option.
See image.
Click Save.
